text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Following privatisation, the Wroclaw-based Pafawag rolling stock maker will employ 1,200 workers. Adtranz, the strategic investor controlled by ABB and Daimler Benz, will buy a 75 percent stake in the plant, raise its capital by $6 million and invest $28.1 million in development in the next six years.
- The EU agreed to allow gradually diminishing protection of Poland's fuel market up to the year 2000, despite Germany's reservations, the EU representatives said.

- The Raciborz-based Rafako boiler maker has won a contract for filtering installation construction in the Siersze power station worth 112 million zlotys, Rafako's deputy president Antoni Szendzielorz said.
- Subscribers of the Centertel analogue mobile network will be able to use their phones in Latvia and Estonia as of December 1 this year, company spokesman Jacek Kalinowski said.

- A group of Polish MPs and telecoms experts criticised the government's longterm telecoms development programme as it did not incorporate proposals for new legal regulations, underrated the needs of internet development, and did not present a forecast of infrastructural changes in the next few years.

- A new oil reloading terminal worth $30 million will be built in the Naftoport oil reloading section of the Gdansk port. The terminal will increase the port's annual reloading capacity by 12 million tonnes.
- The listed Pekpol meat processing firm received a five year development credit of 1.9 million zlotys from state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank.
NOWA EUROPA
- Norway's Gas Negotiating Committee has held talks with the Polish Oil and Gas Company on possible future sale of Norwegian Gas to Poland.
- Poland has become Germany's most important trading partner in central and eastern Europe, leaving Russia behind, Germany's Economy Minister Guenter Rexrodt said.

- A new firm administering the Warsaw-based Okecie airport economic zone will be set up by four local communes in cooperation with the Polskie Porty Lotnicze airport company, the LOT Polish airlines and the Aviation Institute at the beginning of 1997.

- Poland's environmental protection fund (NFOSiGW) and the Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) environmental protection bank will provide a seven years' consortial credit worth 54.7 million zlotys to the Gdansk heat and power plant.
- PZL Swidnik aviation firm has issued two month commercial papers worth 11.46 million zlotys.
- Citroen Poland has issued 35-day commercial papers worth 15 million zlotys.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- In the period from mid-July to mid-October this year only 14 percent of Poland's households had any savings while 27 percent drew loans or credits, a survey by the CBOS polling institute showed.
- The Wedel confectionery maker, controlled by Pepsico, has sold one of its Warsaw-based shops for 2.5 million zlotys.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) plans to invest $20 million in Poland's farming and food production through credits for companies controlled by the listed Rolimpex food processor and trader, the bank said.
ZYCIE
- Poland's auto market is Europe's most receptive, western motor industry experts said. Almost 70 percent of 320,000 cars sold in the country this year were made in Poland.
PARKIET
- The forecast annual net profit of the listed Universal foreign trade company's capital group will be 47 milllion zlotys.
- The Swiecie-based Celuloza paper mill, to be privatised in the near future, has presented the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) with its share issue prospectus.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
